name: Semaglutide
oneLineAnswer: Semaglutide is a prescription GLP-1 medicine, given by injection or by mouth, that lowers blood sugar and body weight.
whatItIs: Semaglutide is a lab-made version of GLP-1, a hormone your gut releases after you eat.
It matches human GLP-1 in 94% of its amino acid sequence.
Small chemical changes at three positions help it resist breakdown and bind to albumin, a blood protein.
That albumin binding is why it leaves the body slowly, with a half-life near one week.
whatItDoes: It switches on the GLP-1 receptor, the same docking site your own GLP-1 hormone uses.
It prompts the pancreas to release insulin when blood sugar is high, and to release less glucagon.
It slows the stomach and reduces appetite, so people in studies ate fewer calories.
Labels say the weight lost is mostly fat mass rather than lean mass.
Adults with type 2 diabetes use it for blood sugar control. Others use it for weight reduction or lower heart risk.
formsAndNames: It comes as an injected liquid and as tablets swallowed by mouth.
Tablet forms include salcaprozate sodium, called SNAC, which helps the peptide get absorbed. Injections do not contain it.
DailyMed lists semaglutide products under the brand names Ozempic, Rybelsus and Wegovy.
Labels say not to combine it with another semaglutide product or any other GLP-1 medicine.
commonSideEffects: Labels list the most common side effects as nausea, abdominal pain, diarrhea, decreased appetite, vomiting and constipation.
Each of those was reported by at least 5% of people in the tablet trials behind the label.
Labels describe some gastrointestinal reactions as severe.
seriousRisksTheLabelsDescribe: Rodents given semaglutide grew thyroid C-cell tumors. Labels say it is unknown whether people would.
Labels say the medicine is not for people with a personal or family history of medullary thyroid carcinoma, or with MEN 2.
Warnings also cover pancreatitis, gallbladder disease, kidney injury from dehydration, diabetic eye complications, and low blood sugar when taken with insulin or sulfonylureas.
whatWeDoNotKnow: Whether the rodent thyroid tumors have any human equivalent. Labels state the human relevance has not been determined.
How the heart benefit actually happens. Labels state the exact mechanism of cardiovascular risk reduction has not been established.
Long-run outcomes beyond trial length. Registry trials ran from months to a few years, with one heart trial following people up to about 240 weeks.
gaps: NCCIH has no semaglutide page. Both https://www.nccih.nih.gov/health/semaglutide and a weight-management NCCIH path returned 404, so no NCCIH grounding is possible for this substance.
No MedlinePlus health topic or medical test summary covered semaglutide. MedlinePlus drug monographs were deliberately not fetched or used.
Numeric trial effect sizes (for example mean percent weight change) were not extracted. Outcome value tables in the ClinicalTrials.gov payload were not read, so no effect size is claimed.
Effects of stopping the medicine, weight regain after stopping, and long-term safety beyond trial follow-up were not grounded in any fetched source.
Cost, insurance coverage, supply shortages, and compounded versions were not grounded and are not described.
Head-to-head comparisons with other GLP-1 medicines were not grounded in any fetched source.

evidence.claim: Semaglutide is a GLP-1 receptor agonist that selectively binds and activates the GLP-1 receptor.
evidence.quote: Semaglutide acts as a GLP-1 receptor agonist that selectively binds to and activates the GLP-1 receptor

evidence.claim: Semaglutide's amino acid sequence is 94% identical to human GLP-1.
evidence.quote: Semaglutide is a GLP-1 analogue with 94% sequence homology to human GLP-1.

evidence.claim: Binding to albumin is the main reason semaglutide lasts so long in the body.
evidence.quote: The principal mechanism of protraction resulting in the long half-life of semaglutide is albumin binding

evidence.claim: Semaglutide also resists breakdown by the DPP-4 enzyme.
evidence.quote: semaglutide is stabilized against degradation by the DPP-4 enzyme

evidence.claim: It lowers blood sugar by raising insulin release and cutting glucagon release, both tied to glucose level.
evidence.quote: it stimulates insulin secretion and lowers glucagon secretion, both in a glucose-dependent manner

evidence.claim: A minor delay in stomach emptying is part of how it lowers blood sugar.
evidence.quote: The mechanism of blood glucose lowering also involves a minor delay in gastric emptying

evidence.claim: Its elimination half-life is about one week.
evidence.quote: Semaglutide elimination half-life is approximately one week

evidence.claim: GLP-1 is a natural regulator of appetite and calorie intake.
evidence.quote: GLP-1 is a physiological regulator of appetite and caloric intake

evidence.claim: The GLP-1 receptor sits in brain areas involved in appetite regulation.
evidence.quote: the GLP-1 receptor is present in several areas of the brain involved in appetite regulation

evidence.claim: Semaglutide lowers calorie intake, and the effect is probably driven by appetite.
evidence.quote: Semaglutide decreases calorie intake. The effects are likely mediated by affecting appetite.

evidence.claim: Weight loss from semaglutide is greater in fat mass than in lean mass.
evidence.quote: Semaglutide lowers body weight with greater fat mass loss than lean mass loss.

evidence.claim: Semaglutide delays stomach emptying.
evidence.quote: Semaglutide delays gastric emptying.

evidence.claim: After the last 2.4 mg dose, semaglutide stays in the bloodstream for roughly five to seven weeks.
evidence.quote: With an elimination half-life of approximately 1 week, semaglutide will be present in the circulation for about 5 to 7 weeks

evidence.claim: The mechanism behind the cardiovascular benefit is not established.
evidence.quote: The exact mechanism of cardiovascular risk reduction has not been established.

evidence.claim: Rodent studies found thyroid C-cell tumors, and human relevance is undetermined.
evidence.quote: In rodents, semaglutide causes thyroid C-cell tumors. It is unknown whether WEGOVY causes thyroid C-cell tumors

evidence.claim: The labels rule out use in people with a personal or family history of medullary thyroid carcinoma or MEN 2.
evidence.quote: WEGOVY is contraindicated in patients with a personal or family history of MTC or in patients with Multiple Endocrine Neoplasia syndrome type 2

evidence.claim: Wegovy is for weight reduction alongside a reduced calorie diet and more physical activity.
evidence.quote: in combination with a reduced calorie diet and increased physical activity

evidence.claim: The labels advise against combining semaglutide with another semaglutide product or any other GLP-1 medicine.
evidence.quote: Coadministration with other semaglutide-containing products or with any other GLP-1 receptor agonist is not recommended

evidence.claim: The most common side effects are digestive, plus decreased appetite, each in at least 5% of trial participants.
evidence.quote: Most common adverse reactions (incidence ≥5%) are nausea, abdominal pain, diarrhea, decreased appetite, vomiting and constipation.

evidence.claim: Some gastrointestinal reactions from the tablets were severe.
evidence.quote: has been associated with gastrointestinal adverse reactions, sometimes severe

evidence.claim: Labels list thyroid C-cell tumor risk and acute pancreatitis among the serious adverse reactions.
evidence.quote: Risk of Thyroid C-cell Tumors [see Warnings and Precautions ( 5.1 )] • Acute Pancreatitis [see Warnings and Precautions ( 5.2 )]

evidence.claim: Semaglutide is indicated as an add-on to diet and exercise for blood sugar control in adults with type 2 diabetes.
evidence.quote: as an adjunct to diet and exercise to improve glycemic control in adults with type 2 diabetes mellitus

evidence.claim: A labeled use is lowering the risk of cardiovascular death, non-fatal heart attack or non-fatal stroke.
evidence.quote: to reduce the risk of major adverse cardiovascular events (cardiovascular death, non-fatal myocardial infarction, or non-fatal stroke)

evidence.claim: That cardiovascular use is limited to adults with type 2 diabetes who are at high risk for these events.
evidence.quote: in adults with type 2 diabetes mellitus who are at high risk for these events

evidence.claim: Tablet forms are oral products containing semaglutide as a GLP-1 receptor agonist.
evidence.quote: RYBELSUS and OZEMPIC tablets, for oral use, contain semaglutide, a GLP-1 receptor agonist

evidence.claim: SNAC (salcaprozate sodium) is listed among the inactive ingredients of the tablet forms.
evidence.quote: the following inactive ingredients: magnesium stearate, microcrystalline cellulose, povidone and salcaprozate sodium (SNAC)

evidence.claim: Position 8 of the peptide is modified so the DPP-4 enzyme cannot degrade it easily.
evidence.quote: modified in position 8 to provide stabilization against degradation by the enzyme dipeptidyl-peptidase 4 (DPP-4)

evidence.claim: A fatty di-acid chain attached at position 26 is what keeps the molecule circulating.
evidence.quote: modification of position 26 lysine with a hydrophilic spacer and a C18 fatty di-acid
